title: Reverse-Engineering Marketplaces
subtitle: Every listed site is a niche someone already proved makes money

items.title: Find an untapped niche
items.text: A low-competition niche, not a guess.

items.title: Replicate a winner
items.text: Find a good competitor in it and replicate what works.

sections.heading: Seven steps, marketplace to validated niche

items.title: Browse marketplaces
items.text: Flippa, Empire Flippers, Motion Invest, FE International.

items.title: Filter for high performers
items.text: Sort by revenue, profit, traffic or growth rate.

items.title: Analyze a promising site
items.text: Ahrefs, SEMrush or Similar Web: SEO, traffic sources, backlinks.

items.title: Check keyword opportunities
items.text: Site Explorer top keywords: high volume, low competition.

items.title: Analyze monetization
items.text: Ads, affiliate, digital products or dropshipping.

items.title: Validate demand and trends
items.text: Google Trends, plus forums, Reddit and Facebook groups.

items.title: Choose and validate
items.text: Consistent demand, more than one monetization option; skip saturated or declining markets.

sections.heading: Reverse-engineering directly: macro site to nano niche

items.title: Macro site
items.text: Open it in Ahrefs Site Explorer

items.title: Nano niche
items.text: One page can point to a niche worth owning

sections.heading: Brand hijacking: four forms to recognise

items.title: Brand keywords
items.text: Content built on a brand name, e.g. "Nike Shoes Review".

items.title: Affiliate hijacking
items.text: Rank for brand terms, redirect to affiliate products.

items.title: Mimicking identity
items.text: Site, logo or content made to resemble a known brand.

items.title: Paid ads on brands
items.text: PPC on a competitor's brand name to intercept clicks.

sections.quote: No dedicated site for the micro-niche? That is the opportunity.
sections.text: Clear intent, high search volume and 12 months of steady Google Trends interest are enough to build one.
